item.title: 贝森特表示，美国新制裁旨在阻止伊朗所有潜在收入来源
item.description:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Monday that new U.S. sanctions aim to block all potential sources of revenue for Iran and told nations to cut economic ties to Tehran or face retaliation.
Bessent said it’s “no longer acceptable to operate in the gray spaces” of the conflict.
He did not name what countries could face potential secondary sanctions from the United States, but China, Turkey and the United Arab Emirates are Iran’s largest trade partners.
“Let there be no ambiguity as to the position of the United States,” Bessent told a news conference. “An economic engagement of any kind with this murderous regime will expose those responsible to the full reach of American power.”
Washington has said the new sanctions aim to put more pressure on aneconomy already batteredby previous sanctions and a U.S. naval blockade.
Bessent made the announcement as Iran’s currency hit a record low.
The rial dropped to 2.02 million to the U.S. dollar as trading opened on currency markets. Iran’s official Central Bank rate stood at around 1.5 million rial to the dollar, but the market rate is what most Iranians pay.
The currency had already been under pressure before the U.S. and Israelattacked Iran on Feb. 28, as Iran faced double-digit inflation and negative growth. The rial has repeatedly hit new lows as nearly six months of war have taken an even greater toll.
Iranians find daily staples increasingly unaffordable. Since the war began, rice is up some 60% and beef prices are more than 150% higher. The International Monetary Fund forecasts that gross domestic product will contract more than 5%.
Still, economic pressure has not yet translated into political pressure. Iran retains akey strategic advantage: Its attacks and threats on ships in theStrait of Hormuzhave brought traffic in the vital waterway to a near halt, damaging the world economy and heaping pressure on U.S. President Donald Trump ahead of congressional elections.
The war, as a result, has devolved into a fight over who controls the strait, through which a fifth of the world’s traded oil transited before the conflict. Iran is now refusing to fully reopen it unless it can charge ships.
Iran and Oman, which is on the opposite side of the strait, are reportedly in thefinal stages of agreeing on a planfor joint management of the waterway. Oman’s foreign minister is set to visit Iran on Tuesday.
In an attempt to break the impasse, the administrationpromised even stronger sanctions, including secondary sanctions on countries that continue to do business with Iran.
Ahead of the announcement, Trump posted on social media that “IRAN IS COMPLETELY COLLAPSING!!!”
“President Trump decimated Iran’s economy to a point where the rial has never been weaker and inflation has rarely been higher,” Bessent wrote Sunday in an opinion piece in the Financial Times. “The regime’s final refuge now lies in the self-deception of fearful nations that still believe accommodating aggression can secure a durable peace.”
Already last week, the United Arab Emirates announced that it wassuspending all tradewith Iran. The UAE has long been one of Iran’s largest trading partners and its biggest source of imports.
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei told reporters in Tehran on Monday that “any escalation of this situation will undoubtedly bring about consequences.”
Pakistan, which played a key role in brokering a 60-day ceasefire in June, sent a high-level delegation to Iran on Monday to encourage the U.S. and Iran to return to negotiations, two senior officials said. The officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the media on the record.
The military confirmed only Field Marshal Asim Munir’s visit, saying it was aimed at deescalating tensions in the region.
Trump spoke with Munir ahead of the army chief’s visit to Iran, according to a person familiar with the discussion. The person spoke on condition of anonymity to confirm a private conversation. Reuters, citing Pakistani sources, first reported the call.
Munir met Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni in Tehran, according to the two senior officials. Munir was accompanied by Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and other officials. Munir was expected to remain in Iran overnight and meet the Iranian president and other senior officials before returning to Pakistan.
His previous visit to Tehran in May helped pave the way for a memorandum of understanding signed by the U.S. and Iran in June.
In downtown Tehran, 73-year-old Sadegh Mahmoudi did not hold out hope for a resolution. He joined a line of about a dozen people to purchase U.S. dollars with his remaining savings to hedge against further declines.
“There is no hope for a deal and peace,” he said.
Amiri reported from New York. Associated Press writers Nasser Karimi in Tehran, Iran; David Rising in Dubai, United Arab Emirates; Seung Min Kim in Washington; and Munir Ahmed in Islamabad contributed.

item.title: 伊朗警告将对预期的美国制裁和其他中东新闻做出严厉反应
item.description:
Iranwarnedthat U.S. sanctions set to be announced Monday would not bring peace to the region. Meanwhile, Israeli and Syrian officials met less than a week after Israelistrikes in Syria. And Israel said it killed a Hamas commander in Gaza.
Here’s a look at the latest developments in theIran warand the wider Middle East on Monday. Full coverage can befound here.
Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson warned that Tehran would respond harshly to expanded U.S. sanctions, including measures against countries it sees as cooperating with Washington.
“Any escalation of this situation will undoubtedly bring about consequences,” Esmail Baghaei said. “Our hands are not tied.” The new head of Iran’s top security body warned Sunday that Tehran will see any country’s support for the sanctions asan “act of war.”
The expanded sanctions come after weeks of impasse. The United States has not dislodged Iran’s grip on theStrait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of the world’s traded oil passed before the war started nearly six months ago.
Iran’s demands for reopening the strait include lifting the U.S. naval blockade, withdrawing U.S. forces from the region and reparations for damages sustained in the war. It has held separate talks with Oman, on the other side of the strait, on jointly managing the waterway regardless of whether a new deal is brokered with the U.S.
Sanctions have historically raised prices of basic goods in Iran, but after decades of withstanding them, Iran’s economy has adapted through finding new trading partners and building domestic industries.
Ahead of the expected U.S. announcement, the country’s currency hit a record low on Monday.
China said Monday that sanctions and additional pressure “will not help resolve the issue,” as the U.S. has threatened toimpose secondary sanctionson countries that trade with Iran.
“They will only exacerbate tensions and escalate the situation, which is in no one’s interest,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said during a daily briefing in Beijing.
He added that China was calling on all parties to avoid measures “that could further intensify differences and conflicts and disrupt global economic development and financial stability.”
China is considered the biggest buyer of Iranian oil, and was importing more than 80% of Iranian oil before the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran.
Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shibani met over the weekend with a high-level Israeli delegation in Jordan to try to defuse tensions after Israel last week struck an air base in northern Syria, Syrian state news agency SANA reported.
The U.S.-mediated discussions on Sunday focused on restarting negotiations for a future security agreement, SANA said.
Israel struck the Abu Duhur air base in Idlib province, saying it aimed to stop Turkey — which has supported the new Syrian government’s efforts to rebuild its armed forces after 14 years of civil war — from establishing a presence there.
Syrian officials during the talks asserted the right to develop an army and freely forge alliances with any country, SANA said.
They also called for the withdrawal of Israeli forces from a buffer zone in southern Syria they have occupied since December 2024, and reiterated Syria’s stance that the Golan Heights — which Israel captured in the 1967 Mideast war and later annexed — is Syrian territory.
Israeli officials didn’t immediately comment on the meeting.
A crude oil tanker was struck by an unknown projectile Monday off Saudi Arabia, the British military said. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Organization said the attack occurred 63 nautical miles west of the Red Sea city of Yanbu, and a fire was ignited on the main deck. There were no reports of casualties.
Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen have attacked Saudi tankers in recent weeks but did not claim this attack, and did not respond to requests for comment. The group’s military spokesperson said the rebels will release a statement about “military operations” later in the day.
Israel’s military said it killed a militant affiliated with Hamas’ special forces unit in an overnight airstrike, the latest targeted killing announced since U.S. officials met with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu last week hoping to push last year’s ceasefire deal forward.
Israel says it targets and kills Palestinian militants it says participated in the Oct. 7, 2023, attack that sparked the war.
Israel has announced targeted strikes on six of the seven days since U.S. negotiator Jared Kushner’s meeting with Netanyahu.
At least 1,288 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire took effect last October, according to Gaza’s health ministry, part of the Hamas-run government. Its numbers are generally considered reliable by the international community.
The Palestinian American homeowner whose residence was besieged this month by Israeli settlers said he remained unable to move freely in the village of Qusra in the occupied West Bank. Loui Riditraveled from Ohioto join his relatives defending his home a week ago.
The Israeli military declared the area a closed zone to restore order in Qusra. Ridi saidsettlers returnedthroughout the week to the hill above his house.
Since Israeli settlers surrounded the house more than two weeks ago, preventing occupants from leaving, Israeli soldiers have encouraged them to leave but Israel’s police have not announced arrests.
The siege and Israel’s response have sparked condemnation from Israeli rights groups and foreign officials, including U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee,who calledthe violence terrorism.
Palestinians consider the West Bank, home to some 3 million Palestinians and 560,000 Israeli settlers, the heart of any future state and have condemned Israel’s expansion there. This year has seen a dramatic spike in violence carried out by Israeli settlers against Palestinians.

item.title: 他正在等待儿子从林肯号航空母舰归来。然后边境巡逻队逮捕了他
item.description:
当路易斯·曼努埃尔·阿维莱斯被移民当局逮捕时，他的儿子在亚伯拉罕·林肯号海军舰艇上服役已进入第九个月，这艘舰艇创下了美国军方在海上不间断停留时间的记录，引发了人们对供应短缺和士兵心理健康状况恶化的担忧。
据路易斯·曼努埃尔·阿维莱斯 (Luis Manuel Aviles) 的妻子阿赫利亚·阿维莱斯 (Argelia Aviles) 称，48 岁的路易斯·曼努埃尔·阿维莱斯 (Luis Manuel Aviles) 在离开家将车开到修理厂后被捕。她说，她的丈夫是佛罗里达州基韦斯特的一名勤杂工，拥有在美国工作的许可证。他来自尼加拉瓜，已在美国生活 19 年。
“他全身心投入工作，这样他才能养家糊口。他是一个好父亲。他全心全意地爱他的孩子们，”47 岁的阿赫利亚说。
阿维莱斯被捕之际，特朗普政府取消了对军人家庭的移民保护，以推行大规模驱逐计划，拘留了至少数十名现役美军的父母和配偶。
美联社在此类拘留的第一份报告中发现，至少有六名家庭成员被驱逐出境，其中一人自行驱逐出境，但政府并未对此进行追踪。美联社报道后，一名美国士兵的妻子在联邦移民拘留所度过了一个多月，她被从飞往巴西的驱逐航班上带走。
军方宣传最多的移民福利之一是“军人就地假释”，它允许现役军人和退伍军人的配偶、子女和父母从国内获得合法移民身份。并非所有人都符合资格：例如，签证逾期或已在边境申请合法身份的人。
美国国土安全部在一份声明中表示，边境巡逻人员周六在基韦斯特逮捕了路易斯·阿维莱斯，在政府寻求驱逐他期间，他将继续被 ICE 拘留。
该部门周日表示，“家庭成员在军队并不是违反我们国家法律的通行证”，并补充说特朗普政府“不会挑选要执行的法律”。
阿维莱斯的儿子在脸书上发帖称，他在部署在中东的林肯号航空母舰上已经连续 250 多天实行 12 小时轮班制，没有休息。此次部署引发了人们的广泛担忧，包括对长期远离陆地的军人的影响、食品短缺以及船舶及其设备日益增加的压力。
五角大楼将所有问题转交给海军。周日下午，海军没有立即回复通过电子邮件发送的置评请求。国防部长皮特·赫格斯此前称林肯号上的情况“完全被歪曲”。
约书亚·阿维莱斯在周六的帖子中写道，周六早上他接到关于父亲被拘留的电话时，他仍在林肯号航空母舰上“为一个给予我一切的国家而战”。
约书亚·阿维利斯写道：“这让我心碎。我不知道我怎么能在精神上继续每天工作 12 个多小时，因为我知道我的父亲在某个地方，可能会被当作罪犯对待。”
约书亚·阿维莱斯 (Joshua Aviles) 的妹妹、28 岁的凯瑟琳·德尔加多 (Katherine Delgado) 表示，约书亚参军的部分原因是他认为这会提高他父亲获得公民身份的机会，这样他就“不再生活在被捕的恐惧中”。
她说，与约书亚分开对她来说是毁灭性的打击，她称约书亚是她“最好的朋友”，也是她的“不骑就死”。
“我花了好几个星期都不知道他在哪里，”德尔加多说。她说，当她收到他的消息并被告知他没有得到足够的食物时，她花了数百美元给他寄了装有食品和卫生用品的护理包，其中一些从未到达。
德尔加多说，约书亚“应该很快就会回家”，指的是有消息称她哥哥所乘坐的船将很快在中东停止使用。“他会在没有父亲的情况下回家。”
据路易斯·阿维莱斯的妻子说，儿子的长期部署对路易斯·阿维莱斯来说是一个挑战。他告诉她，他期待着部署最终结束。她说，六个月过去了，儿子还没有回来，阿维利斯心烦意乱。
“他很兴奋，”她说。“他想拥抱他的儿子，因为他已经九个月没见到他了。”

item.title: 律师称，因杀害索尼娅·马西而被定罪的伊利诺伊州前副议员肖恩·格雷森在监狱中去世
item.description:
芝加哥（美联社）——周日，伊利诺伊州前副警长肖恩·格雷森（Sean Grayson）在服刑 20 年期间去世，他在家中枪杀索尼娅·马西（Sonya Massey），成为警方使用武力的焦点。
格雷森的律师丹尼尔·富尔茨证实，他的当事人周日早些时候去世，但拒绝提供任何进一步的细节。
32 岁的格雷森于 10 月份枪杀了一名 36 岁的黑人妇女梅西，被判犯有二级谋杀罪。梅西举报称，她在斯普林菲尔德地区的家外可能有一名潜行者。2024 年 7 月那次遭遇的随身摄像机视频显示，梅西蹲在厨房里道歉，随后格雷森向她的脸部开枪。
他于一月份被判处最高 20 年监禁。
格雷森在梅西被杀之前就被诊断出患有结肠癌，他的律师在宣判他时表示，这种疾病已经扩散到他的肝脏和肺部。今年五月，在服刑仅几个月后，他就根据伊利诺伊州法律为患有绝症或严重健康状况的囚犯寻求医疗释放。伊利诺伊州囚犯审查委员会上个月拒绝了他的请求。
2024 年 7 月 6 日早些时候，Massey 拨打了 911，报告有人在她家外面徘徊。格雷森和另一位桑加蒙县副警长做出了回应。
视频显示，格雷森指导梅西从炉子中取出一壶热水。当她拿着锅时，梅西告诉代表们：“我奉耶稣的名责备你们。”
格雷森威胁要开枪打死她，并拔出手枪，命令她放下锅。在格雷森连开三枪之前，梅西道歉并躲到厨房柜台后面。
另一位副手道森·法利后来作证说，他并不认为梅西是威胁，只有在格雷森拔出武器后，他才拔出了自己的武器。
格雷森在枪击事件后被解雇，并被指控犯有一级谋杀罪。在格雷森辩称他担心梅西会向他泼热水后，陪审团判定他犯有较轻的二级谋杀罪。
梅西被杀引起了全国关注和抗议，并引发了人们对格雷森在被桑加蒙县治安官办公室雇用之前如何通过多个执法机构的质疑。
伊利诺伊州立法者后来通过了《索尼娅·梅西法案》，要求执法机构在雇用官员之前更仔细地审查申请人以前的就业记录。
梅西去世后，司法部还启动了民权调查，随后与桑加蒙县、治安官办公室和其他机构达成协议，要求改变警务和应急响应。这些变化包括与行为健康障碍人士互动的额外培训以及制定移动危机应对计划。

item.title: 两名凤凰城警察在暴力、未报告的交通堵塞后被捕并被解雇
item.description:
菲尼克斯（美联社）——警察局长说，菲尼克斯市的两名警察在一次未报告的交通堵塞中袭击了一名男子和一名女子，并用泰瑟枪电击他们，随后被解雇并被捕。
警察局长马特·乔达诺在周六的新闻发布会上表示，警官安东尼奥·菲利克斯和路易斯·瓦斯奎兹因严重袭击和绑架等罪名被捕。
佐丹奴说：“侦探们已经证实，这两名前警官在交通堵塞期间对这名男子和女子进行了人身攻击。”“调查还显示，在拦截过程中，有人对受害者使用了泰瑟枪。”
警方称，警察没有报告 8 月 5 日的交通堵塞，也没有启动随身携带的摄像头。
佐丹奴说：“没有视频证据，但我们确定了我们认为犯下这些罪行的可能原因。”他补充说，没有迹象表明警察认识受害者。
马里科帕县治安官办公室发言人戴夫·埃文斯周日表示，瓦斯奎兹已被释放，而菲利克斯仍被监禁在凤凰城的下七叶树监狱。
美联社试图确定谁是他们的辩护律师来请求发表评论，但没有成功。
凤凰城警方的一份声明称，在凤凰城深夜的交通堵塞中，男司机和女乘客报告称，警察砸碎了车窗。瓦斯奎兹殴打了这名男子，并威胁要开枪射击他，而这名女子则被带下车并戴上手铐。
声明称，这名男子设法开车离开，并将汽车遗弃在邻近的坦佩，而女子则在现场被释放。
根据坦佩警方的报告，邻近坦佩的一名警官对这辆被遗弃的汽车做出了回应，询问该车是否从邻近的警察机构逃离，并被告知没有。
坦佩警官给这辆车的登记车主、男司机的母亲打电话，通过她联系上了女乘客，最终联系上了男司机。女乘客告诉警官，两人都被泰瑟枪电击，而男子后来告诉警官，他的脸部被多次殴打，他们多次询问为何被拦住。
坦佩警官在报告中写道，他相信他们是冒充警察企图劫车的受害者。
凤凰城警察局长佐丹奴表示，当他最初得知这起事件时，也有类似的反应，因为这“远远超出了我们政策的范围”。但他说，当侦探们开始调查此事时，他们意识到凤凰城警官可能参与其中，并将此案转为特别调查细节。
“从那时起，他们开始收集证据，包括自动车辆定位器，该定位器确实在受害者报告事件发生时将车辆放置在该位置，”佐丹奴说，他指的是城市车辆中的定位技术。
瓦斯奎兹和菲利克斯分别在凤凰城警察局工作了八年和九年。佐丹奴没有详细说明，但表示两人此前都违反了部门政策，但“并非如此”。
凤凰城部门的调查和审计正在进行中。官员们定于周五开庭。

item.title: 卡尼表示，特朗普的要求将摧毁加拿大汽车业，而福特则警告美国可能会被切断
item.description:
TORONTO (AP) — Prime Minister Mark Carney said Monday thatU.S. trade demandsconfirmed Canada’s fears that U.S. President Donald Trump was seeking to dismantle its auto industry, as Trump threatened new 50% tariffs on Canadian vehicles, auto parts and steel, and as Ontario Premier Doug Ford warned Canada could cut off electricity and critical minerals to the United States.
Carney said Canada remained willing to negotiate, but only if Washington approached the talks as a partnership between sovereign countries. He said “an attitude at the negotiation table that Canada is a subsidiary of the United States” is “not something we’re going to accept.”
Ford, speaking in an interview with The Associated Press, said Trump has underestimated Canadians’ willingness to endure economic pain rather than give in to U.S. pressure.
“He underestimates Canada. We’re all in,” Ford said. “Up here, we’re at a fever pitch, everyone’s in for an economic war. They know they’re going to have to sacrifice.”
Trump said Monday that the new 50% tariffs on Canadian automobiles, auto parts and steel would begin next year.
“Canada has been ripping off the United States of America for years,” Trump wrote on social media, criticizing what he called Canada’s “ridiculously high tariffs” on American farmers.
Carney said Washington’s auto-sector proposals would “gradually dismantle” Canadian production.
Carney noted Canada is the largest customer for U.S. automobiles and questioned what Trump’s latest move would mean for workers in states such as Ohio, Kentucky and Alabama who depend on Canadian demand.
“This is the most successful automotive partnership in history,” Carney said, referring to the deeply integrated Canada-U.S. industry.

Carneywalked away from trade negotiations with the Trump administration late Friday, sayingWashington demanded too muchin exchange for tariff relief. The United States imposed 50% tariffs Saturday on about $20 billion worth of Canadian goods, while Carney announced dollar-for-dollar retaliation beginning Sept. 8.
In the AP interview, Ford said Trump had “declared war, economic war againsthis closest friendand ally” before invoking Ronald Reagan, whose opposition to tariffs Ford previously featured in a television advertising campaign aimed at Americans.
Ford noted that Trump keeps a portrait of the late president near his desk.
“He’d be throwing up on him from the picture if he knew what was going on, spinning around in his grave right now,” Ford said. “He should maybe take that picture off the wall and move it somewhere else. Because right now, Ronald Reagan would be disgusted with President Trump.”
The White House responded to Ford’s criticisms by noting that Reagan took similar actions toward Japan that Trump was doing to Canada.
“President Reagan enacted a 100% tariff on Japanese electronics for dumping on the U.S. market and failing to open up Japan’s market to Made-in-USA goods,” White House spokesman Kush Desai said.
Ford, a Progressive Conservative, is from a different party than Carney, a Liberal, underscoring the broad political unity in Canada over the trade fight with Trump.
Ford said “everything is on the table” if the dispute worsens, including cutting off electricity and critical minerals from Ontario. He also called for Canada to consider using oil and potash as leverage.
“I’ll cut them off,” Ford said of critical minerals. “You won’t get a grain of sand out of Ontario.”
Critical minerals are increasingly important to U.S. national security and manufacturing. The Pentagon has sought more secure supplies of minerals used in military aircraft, missiles, munitions and electronics as Washington tries to reduce reliance on China, which dominates the mining or processing of several strategically important minerals.
Ford specifically cited high-grade nickel shipped to the United States and uranium refined in Ontario.
“What would they do without the high-grade nickel that we ship down to the U.S.?” Ford said.
Ford said Canada should consider increasingly severe retaliation if Trump continues targeting Canadian industries, including oil and potash, while Ontario could raise electricity prices or stop sending power south.
“We power 1.5 million homes and businesses,” Ford said. “Everything’s on the table. I’ll do whatever it takes.”
If Trump continues trying to dismantle Canadian manufacturing, Ford said, “he better have a pack of batteries.”
Ford has used electricity as leverage before. During an earlier phase of the dispute, Ontario imposed a 25% surcharge on electricity exported to Michigan, Minnesota and New York. Trump responded by threatening to double tariffs on Canadian steel and aluminum before both sides backed away.
Ford accused Trump of seeking not simply a better trade deal but to hollow out Canadian industries and move production south.
Ford said Trump wants to make Canada a vassal state.
“He wants to bleed out every single sector and bring them down to the U.S.,” Ford said.
The auto sector is especially important to Ontario, the center of Canada’s vehicle manufacturing industry. Plants and suppliers in Ontario are tightly integrated with factories in Michigan and other U.S. states, with parts routinely crossing the border multiple times during production.
Automakers including Ford, General Motors and Stellantis operate major assembly plants in Ontario, and the wider supply chain supports tens of thousands of jobs. Trump’s new threat of a 50% tariff on Canadian vehicles and parts puts that sector directly at the center of the escalating dispute.
U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said Monday that “the only reason Canada has auto production in the first place” was because of the 1960s Auto Pact, under which Canada used access to its market to encourage vehicle production north of the border.
“If he thinks the Canadian people are going to roll over and just continue buying American-made vehicles, it’s not going to happen,” Ford said.
Ford also disclosed that he had opposed the preliminary agreement Carney was considering before Canada walked away from the negotiations.
“I wasn’t supporting the deal,” Ford said.
Ford said he was unwilling to restore American liquor to Ontario store shelves as part of an agreement and had been prepared to publicly break with the proposed deal.
“I wasn’t going to put the booze back on the shelves,” Ford said. “I was ready to go out there and call a press conference ... and say I’m not buckling over.”
Ford said he understood Washington had sought language late in the negotiations that would have restricted Canada’s ability to negotiate trade agreements with other countries without U.S. approval. Carney has called that demand unacceptable and a question of Canadian sovereignty.
“Who does he think he is?” Ford said of Trump. “You gotta be kidding.”
Ford’s Reagan comments revived an earlier clash with Trump. Last year, Ontario paid for U.S. television advertisements featuring excerpts from a 1987 Reagan address warning that tariffs can provoke retaliation and trade wars.
Trump accused Ontario of misrepresenting Reagan and abruptly ended trade negotiations with Canada. Ford later agreed to pause the campaign so talks could resume.
Yet despite the increasingly hostile talk, Ford said Canada should remain willing to negotiate.
“I never believe in walking away from the table,” Ford said. “Continue negotiating and see where we go.”
Associated Press writer Seung Min Kim contributed from Washington.

item.title: 贾里德·库什纳 (Jared Kushner) 于 11 月会见民主党领袖杰弗里斯 (Jeffries)，众议院控制权岌岌可危
item.description:
WASHINGTON (AP) — HouseDemocratic leader Hakeem Jeffriesand President Donald Trump’s son-in-law and outside adviserJared Kushnermet privately recently in New York, a signal that the White House is seeking ways to work with Democrats if they wrest majority control from Republicans in themidterm elections.
The meeting, first reported Sunday by The New York Times, touched on issues ranging from housing, immigration to the high costs of living. People in the United States are struggling under inflationary prices that Democrats blame on Republicans, alongside Trump, for failing to get under control.
Kushner suggested that Jeffries, who isin line to become House speakerif Democrats regain power in November, meet with White House chief of staff Susie Wiles as a follow-up.
Jeffries, in a statement Sunday, did not mention the private conversation but said the Republican administration needed to drop the GOP’s “my-way-or-the-highway” approach that “has failed the American people.”
“To stop the madness, we have repeatedly made clear that an extremist approach will not work and will be met with forceful opposition,” the New York congressman said. “The question is whether Republicans will join us.”
The meeting shows the depth of Republican Party angst over losingtheir congressional majority, particularly the House, and the need to make inroads with the opposing party as the White House seeks to stem any potential political fallout on the president.
If Democrats retake power, the White House can expect anaggressive oversight agendainto what Jeffries has called the “crooks” in the administration, with the threat of impeachment among the many tools at the party’s disposal.
House Speaker Mike Johnson, a close ally of Trump, bristled Sunday when asked about the meeting. He minimized the role that Kushner, who he said “hedges his bets,” plays in the White House.

“I’m telling you what, you better not bet against the House Republicans,” Johnson, R-La., told Fox News Channel’s “The Sunday Briefing.”
“I don’t know what that’s about,” Johnson said. “I know Jared has interests in lots of other things going on. He’s not really directly involved in the admin, at least in the day-to-day in the White House.”
The White House did not respond to a request for comment. A representative for Kushner also did not respond.
The New Yorkers allied during the first Trump administration onlandmark legislationto allow sentencing flexibility for certain drug offenses as a way to curtail lengthy terms in the federal prison system.
While not necessarily close, the two have maintained a relationship despite the repeated attacks Trump has leveled against Jeffries and the Democratic leader’s responses. In Trump’s second term, Kushner has an oversize role despite having no formal position in the White House. He serves as an outside adviser and envoy, particularlyshuttling to foreign diplomatic missionsas theU.S. war against Irandrags into its sixth month.
Trump has onlymet with Jeffries oncesince the president returned to the White House, taunting the House leader and Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer of New York with red “Make America Great Again” 2028 caps on the desk in front of them in the Oval Office — a nod to Trump’s toying with an unconstitutional third term in office.
After that fall meeting, Trump posted a fake image of Schumer with Jeffries wearing a sombrero with a handlebar mustache in what was widely viewed as aracist tropeas he mocked the Democrats before what became thelongest federal government shutdownin U.S. history.
Trump has been able to alternately ignore the Congress as he relies on the sheer force of executive power to implement his priorities or to pressure the Republicans in the House and Senate, when needed, to fall in line behind the White House, particularly to confirm controversial Cabinet nominees.
All that is likely to change if Democrats control either chamber, with lawmakers eager for Congress to flex their own power as a coequal branch of government more willing to hold the White House in check.
House Republicans are counting on Trump’s popularity among their core voters as they struggle to hold onto majority control, with Johnson believing the GOP will defy history that tends to reward the challengers in midterms and punish the party in power.
The House GOP has a slim majority. Control will likely be won — or lost — in a handful of battleground districts as Democrats put forward candidates in what they hope will be something of a repeat of 2018, when they swept to power riding a wave of voter unrest during Trump’s first term.
While the House is most at risk for Republicans this year, he narrowly split Senate is also increasingly in play. GOP strategists worry about an enthusiasm gap on their side as Democrats appear more eager to head to the polls.
At the same time, Democrats are nominating outsider candidates, some aligned with socialist agendas over establishment backed candidates, in a sign of voter unrest with the status quo.
Associated Press writer Michelle L. Price contributed to this report.

item.title: Enes Kanter Freedom 在与 Sky's Cloud 对抗后被逐出 Fever-Sky 比赛
item.description:
芝加哥（美联社）——前 NBA 中锋埃内斯·坎特·弗里德姆 (Enes Kanter Freedom) 在周日晚上的印第安纳-芝加哥 WNBA 比赛第三节末与天空队后卫娜塔莎·克劳德 (Natasha Cloud) 发生冲突后被驱逐出场。
自由就在底线。他穿着一件黑色衬衫，上面写着“女人名词。成年人类女性”。
第三节还剩 1 分 22 秒时，克劳德内线得分，狂热队请求暂停。随后，克劳德与队友艾莎·库利巴利碰了碰胸部，然后转身朝坎特的方向走去。
当 34 岁的坎特走近时，34 岁的克劳德开始大喊大叫，并指着 34 岁的坎特。站着的坎特张开双臂，在球场上迈出了一步，保安和几名天空队球员走到了两人之间。
“只是发生了一起球迷事件，保安人员处理了此事，我们只会专注于比赛，”芝加哥前锋阿祖拉·史蒂文斯在天空队以 113-90 失利后说道。
芝加哥队主教练泰勒·马什表示，克劳德担心会分散球队的注意力。
“我告诉她她不是，”马什说。“我告诉她，我们都拥护她，因为她会保护我们的团队并保护需要保护的人，因此塔什将始终坚持这一点，我们代表塔什。”
自由在篮筐附近停下来，在被护送出球场区域时向保安陈述自己的情况。他一边转身，一边伸出衬衫，鼓励人群做出回应，然后他走向前厅。
在离开 Wintrust Arena 之前，他与一群警察进行了交谈。
“我没有看到，我们正在讨论下一场比赛，”印第安纳球星凯特琳·克拉克说，“所以我认为这可能是芝加哥的一个问题。”
克劳德赛后会见了球队和联盟的保安。她没有接受媒体采访。
最近，WNBA 一直是关于是否应该允许跨性别女性（出生时被指定为男性，但为了适应自己的性别认同而转变）的辩论的主题。WNBA从来没有出现过这样的球员。
尽管联盟的集体谈判协议规定 WNBA 仅限女性参加，但它没有包含有关性别认同或出生性别的更具体的语言。
发烧卫士索菲·坎宁安 (Sophie Cunningham) 在上个月发布的 ESPN 简介中表示，她反对跨性别女孩和妇女参加女子和女子运动项目。自由和另一位前 NBA 球员罗伊斯·怀特 (Royce White) 宣布自己有资格参加 WNBA 选秀，称自己是女性。
赛前，坎特在场外参加了一场小型集会，支持坎宁安。
当被问及是否有什么话想对坎特说时，马什赞扬了联盟及其球员。
“如果你来观看一场比赛，你可能应该来享受篮球，”他说，“这对我来说似乎很简单。我认为这些球员应得的，并且已经赢得了。作为一名前篮球运动员，你可能也应该理解并感受到这一点。”

item.title: 谢夫勒称自己患有手足口病参加宝马锦标赛
item.description:
英石。路易斯（美联社）——斯科蒂·舍夫勒在宝马锦标赛中吞下本周第 13 个柏忌，以他的标准来看，这是一场最普通的表现。事实证明，考虑到他的健康状况，这是最不寻常的一周。
“我病了，”谢夫勒周四拒绝采访请求时说道。
周日，舍夫勒以 68 杆，低于标准杆 2 杆的成绩结束比赛后，他提供了更多细节。他说他正在治疗会引起水泡的手足口病。
“所以从本周开始，握球杆是非常痛苦的，”他说。“如果我更聪明的话，也许我会退出，但我打得很好，我觉得如果我能快速淘汰并通过前几轮，我仍然有机会。”
舍夫勒在联邦快递圣裘德锦标赛上以八杆优势取得胜利，似乎在美巡赛赛季结束三周的正确时间里迈出了步伐。
事后看来，谢夫勒表示，在风险如此小的情况下退出是谨慎的做法。他已经通过宝马锦标赛确定了联邦快递杯第一名，这为他赢得了2300万美元的奖金。下周的巡回锦标赛上，种子队甚至都不重要，因为所有晋级的 30 名选手只需在东湖获胜即可夺得联邦快递杯。
“我认为这可能是我固执的一部分。这可能是我的优点，有时也是缺点，”舍夫勒说。“我从来没有退出过比赛，尤其是在比赛中途。这对我来说真的很令人沮丧。
“但我为自己的战斗方式感到自豪，”他说。“感觉我开始痊愈了。我的喉咙仍然困扰着我。但今天我的手感觉正常。”
他唯一的错误——除了三个柏忌——是在比赛结束时差点与卡梅伦·杨握手，因为他感觉已经恢复正常了。
谢夫勒连续抓到三只小鸟，短暂进入前十名，但他在球道沙坑吞下柏忌。舍夫勒本周的果岭率仅为 65%。
“随着这一周的过去，我感觉好多了，”他说。“周一晚上我生病了。这可能是最令人沮丧的部分。打一场非常好的高尔夫球，你会从炎热中走出来，得到一点肾上腺素，有时你的身体会崩溃。然后整个星期我都受到了很好的打击。
“我现在还没有100%恢复，但我现在会休息一下，希望这会有所帮助。”

item.title: 凯特琳·克拉克拿下37分，狂热队以113-90击败天空队
item.description:
芝加哥（美联社）——周日晚上，凯特琳·克拉克拿下 37 分，凯尔西·米切尔拿下 30 分，帮助印第安纳热队以 113-90 战胜芝加哥天空队。
克拉克投中了印第安纳队队史纪录的 18 个三分球中的职业生涯最高的 8 个。她还有10次助攻。
狂热队以 3-2 结束了四晚第三场比赛。他们已经连续丢了两个。
娜塔莎·克劳德 (Natasha Cloud) 为芝加哥队拿下 16 分和 7 次助攻，帮助球队取得三连胜。阿祖拉·史蒂文斯得到 14 分和 8 个篮板。
天空队因周日晚上的失利和华盛顿队的胜利而被淘汰出季后赛。
印第安纳队中锋阿利亚·波士顿因右腿受伤缺席比赛。波士顿在周六以 109-102 输给纽约的比赛中拿下 22 分和 6 次助攻。
第三节热队打出一波13-2的高潮，以71-60领先。克拉克以三分开始冲刺，米切尔连拿八分，克拉克在比赛还剩 4 分 31 秒时跳投结束比赛。
比赛还剩 4 分 37 秒时，莱克西·赫尔 (Lexie Hull) 反向上篮将比分改写为 97-82。赫尔城队为热队拿下14分，马凯拉·廷普森拿下12分。
这是自 8 月 8 日热火队以 90-86 获胜的第一节印第安纳后卫索菲·坎宁安 (Sophie Cunningham) 因严重犯规被迪乔奈·卡林顿 (DiJonai Carrington) 放倒以来，这是两队之间的第一场比赛。坎宁安在上场超过 11 分钟的时间里拿下三分，而天空队的卡林顿在 18 分钟内得到了 7 分。
前NBA中锋埃内斯·坎特·弗里德姆(Enes Kanter Freedom)出席了比赛，但他在第三节与克劳德对抗后被驱逐出场。自由和另一位前 NBA 球员罗伊斯·怀特 (Royce White) 宣布自己有资格参加 WNBA 选秀，称自己是女性。
周五晚上，狂热队将主场迎战康涅狄格太阳队。
天空电视台周二晚上访问康涅狄格州。

item.title: 《Johnny Angel》歌手、《Donna Reed Show》和《Coach》演员雪莱·法巴雷斯 (Shelley Fabares) 去世，享年 82 岁
item.description:
雪莱·法巴雷斯 (Shelley Fabares) 去世了，她是一位演员，从十几岁的时候就出演过《唐娜·里德秀》，一直到《一次的一天》和《教练》，数十年来一直在电视上崭露头角。她82岁了。
她的家人在给美联社的一份声明中说，她周六在洛杉矶去世。没有给出原因。
“对于她的家人和朋友来说，雪莱是爱、力量、欢笑和安慰的源泉，”她的家人写道。“她有一种非凡的能力，能让人们感到受欢迎、受到重视和关心。”
法巴雷斯 1944 年出生于加利福尼亚州圣莫尼卡，年幼时就开始演艺事业。她的第一个电视作品出现在 10 岁时，当时她出现在“Loretta Young Show”节目中。随后出现了许多电影和电视节目：她与保罗·纽曼、弗兰克·西纳特拉和爱娃·玛丽·圣特一起出演了制片人展示制作的《我们的小镇》；曾出演罗莎琳德·拉塞尔 (Rosalind Russell) 的电影《女孩拉什》(The Girl Rush) 和罗克·哈德森 (Rock Hudson) 的戏剧《永不说再见》(Never Say Goodbye)。其他早期作品包括《安妮特》、《午夜船长》和《阴阳魔界》的《黑色皮夹克》一集。
她最大的突破是在《唐娜·里德秀》中饰演玛丽·斯通，从 1958 年到 1963 年，她一直是该节目的常客。在那段时间里，她还获得了一份唱片合同，并制作了两首热门 40 首单曲，其中包括《约翰尼·天使》。20 世纪 60 年代初，她还与埃尔维斯·普雷斯利 (Elvis Presley) 共同主演了三部电影：《Girl Happy》、《Spinout》和《Clambake》。
“我认为《唐娜·里德秀》中的那些年，从 14 岁到 19 岁，是非常重要的，”法巴雷斯 1993 年告诉《洛杉矶时报》。“唐娜·里德是一位非凡的女性，一位充满力量、善良、正直和同情心的女性。我并不是想让她听起来像个圣人，但她对我的影响最为深远。我今天带着她。”
20 世纪 70 年代末，法巴雷斯在 CBS 情景喜剧“One Day at a Time”中饰演弗朗辛·韦伯斯特 (Francine Webster)，给人留下了深刻的印象。她还在《布莱恩之歌》中扮演詹姆斯·凯恩的妻子。她最重要的角色之一是在《教练》中饰演克里斯汀·阿姆斯特朗，尽管该剧花了一分钟才找到观众。
“我从一开始就一直觉得，如果他们能为我们找到合适的地点，这就是一场能够持续下去的演出，”她在 1993 年接受《洛杉矶时报》采访时说道。
法巴雷斯结过两次婚，第一次是 1964 年与制片人卢·阿德勒 (Lou Adler) 结婚。自 1984 年起，她与《M-A-S-H》演员迈克·法雷尔 (Mike Farrell) 结婚。她还是阿尔茨海默氏症意识的忠实倡导者，这影响了她的母亲。
1999年初，她因食道出血而去急诊室检查，结果发现她患有进行性肝功能衰竭。在等待名单上等待了 22 个月后，她于 2000 年 10 月接受了肝移植手术。
移植三年后，她在洛杉矶西达斯-西奈医疗中心接受采访时表示，她“因这次经历而改变”，并永远感激法雷尔“一路走来”的陪伴。
她的家人在声明中表示，“我们将记住雪莱的善良、忠诚、机智、勇气和美丽的精神。我们将深深地怀念她——不仅是作为一位著名的表演者，而且作为我们日常生活中充满爱心和非凡的人。”

item.title: 《蜘蛛侠》第四周末票房冠军《奥德赛》成为诺兰票房最高的电影
item.description:
《蜘蛛侠：崭新的一天》击败了包括喜剧片、恐怖片、杰森·斯坦森动作片和家庭片在内的一大批新片，在上映第四周保持了票房第一的位置。《奥德赛》也成为克里斯托弗·诺兰有史以来票房最高的电影，无论是国内还是国际。
据电影公司周日估计，今年《奥德赛》仅次于《蜘蛛侠》，美国和加拿大的 4,006 家影院为《蜘蛛侠》增加了 3,900 万美元的票房收入。《蜘蛛侠》目前在北美的票房收入已超过 8.549 亿美元，很快将超越《复仇者联盟：终局之战》，成为有史以来第二高的国内电影票房。目前的纪录保持者是《星球大战：原力觉醒》（9.367 亿美元）。
索尼还推出了周末第二大电影《潜伏：超越》。该系列的第六部电影由 Blumhouse Atomic Monster 制作，在 3,303 家影院上映，票房收入达 2,530 万美元。在国际上，它赚了3500万美元。其 1800 万美元的制作预算使其成为该系列中最昂贵的电影。
第三名是《奥德赛》，该片本周早些时候超越了《死侍与金刚狼》，成为有史以来票房最高的 R 级电影。该片在北美影院上映的第六个周末票房收入增加了 1,950 万美元，并继续在 3,000 多个地点上映，使其国内总票房接近 5.391 亿美元。这使得《黑暗骑士》的票房收入突破了 5.349 亿美元——这是诺兰之前的最高纪录——不考虑通货膨胀。在国际方面，它增加了 6800 万美元，主要由中国和韩国推动，使其全球总美元达到 14 亿美元。
其他大牌新人的排名进一步下滑。《叛变》由斯坦森主演，饰演一名被错误指控谋杀其亿万富翁老板的男子，该片在 2,703 个地点上映，票房收入 750 万美元，排名第六。狮门影业发行（收购）的目的是只在院线上映，但在上映前几天，它意外地在 Prime Video 上免费播放了几个小时，然后错误才得到纠正。这个故障可能影响了首映周末的收入，但影片也有一些相当糟糕的评论。
评价更差的是《温泉周末》，这是一部由《宿醉》和《坏妈妈》背后的男人们创作的一部女孩旅行喜剧，由艾拉·菲舍尔、莱斯利·曼、安娜·法瑞丝和米歇尔·布托主演。该片在 2,009 个地点的收入预计为 310 万美元。据 PostTrak 称，在周末开放门票购买者中，女性约占 84%。《速度与激情》25周年纪念版的重映赚得稍微多一些。
由安德鲁·加菲尔德 (Andrew Garfield) 主演的《遥远的魔法树》(The Magic Faraway Tree) 在 1,611 块银幕上上映，票房收入 140 万美元，超出了前十名。
然而，安东尼·波登 (Anthony Bourdain) 的年轻电影《托尼》(Tony) 仍然表现出色，在 1,652 块银幕上获得了 500 万美元的票房收入。
截至劳动节的夏季门票收入目前在北美已创造了约 44 亿美元的收入，跻身有史以来票房收入最高的四个夏季门票之列。
Rentrak 市场趋势主管保罗·德加拉贝迪安 (Paul Dergarabedian) 表示：“我认为，我们正处于票房历史上最重要、最关键的夏季电影季之一的冲刺阶段。”“我不知道今年夏天如何复制。工作室会尝试的。”
电影院贸易组织 Cinema United 的总裁兼首席执行官迈克尔·奥利里 (Michael O’Leary) 指出，市场上种类繁多的电影为暑期档的上映做出了贡献。他告诉美联社，部分原因是该行业终于从 2023 年好莱坞罢工的影响中恢复过来。
“坦率地说，最令我兴奋的是电影观众的热情，”奥利里说。“当你去剧院时，你会感受到这一点。在剧院里有一种最近从未有过的能量。”
今年总体也超过了 70 亿美元，比 2025 年增长约 20.4%，但比 2019 年落后约 7.1%。

item.title: 华尔街在本周可能会波动股票和债券的重要一周前出现波动
item.description:
纽约（美联社）——周一，美国股市出现波动，接下来的一周可能会发生一些可能影响市场的事件。与此同时，美国财政部试图平息的债券市场领域有所放松。
标准普尔 500 指数下跌 0.3%，较本月初创下的历史高点进一步回落。截至下午 1 点 42 分，道琼斯工业平均指数上涨 59 点，即 0.1%。东部时间，纳斯达克综合指数下跌0.6%。
由于担心人工智能技术的狂热导致价格过高，以及如果不能产生足够的利润，对人工智能芯片的巨大需求将无法持续，科技股在夏季大幅波动后一路下跌。
芯片巨头英伟达是人工智能热潮的巨大赢家，并因此成为华尔街最大、最具影响力的股票。该公司将于周三发布最新的季度收益报告，这可能决定人工智能相关股票的下一个重大走势。
英伟达股价下跌 2.3%，是标准普尔 500 指数中权重最大的公司，该指数大部分股票均上涨。美光科技 (Micron Technology) 下跌 6%，博通 (Broadcom) 下跌 2%，也拖累该指数走低。
最近影响股市的另一个重要因素是债券市场，由于对高通胀、巨额政府债务和其他因素的担忧，长期国债收益率在整个夏季攀升。高收益率使每个人（而不仅仅是政府）的借贷成本变得更高，并且已经推高了抵押贷款利率并损害了房地产业。
美国财政部上周出人意料地宣布增加计划回购美国国债的规模，这可能有助于遏制10年期和30年期美国国债收益率的上升。但分析师警告称，此举可能只会产生有限的效果，因为回购规模太小，而且无法解决美国政府债务过高和伊朗战争导致的油价昂贵等根本问题。
华尔街在早盘交易中表现不佳。
周一，10 年期国债收益率从周五晚间的 4.74% 降至 4.70%，并回到周二晚间美国财政部意外宣布之前的水平。
周一油价下跌导致收益率下降。布伦特原油下跌 2.3%，至每桶 90.55 美元。
上个月，随着人们对美国和伊朗能够达成协议，允许油轮再次自由离开波斯湾的希望不断上升和下降，美元汇率在 72 美元和 102 美元之间波动。尽管美国宣布对伊朗实施新的制裁，导致伊朗货币价值跌至历史新低。
尽管周一收益率有所下降，但分析师警告称，美国政府影响债券市场的尝试最终可能意味着通胀压力加大。多年来，通货膨胀率已经高于几乎所有人的预期。
这增加了美联储提高联邦基金利率的压力，从而影响了非常短期的隔夜贷款。当美联储提高利率时，它可以通过试图减缓整体经济并降低股票和其他投资的价格来帮助抑制通货膨胀。
美联储新任主席凯文·沃什将于周五在怀俄明州杰克逊霍尔举行的经济研讨会上发表讲话。过去，山区环境一直是美联储发布重大政策公告的背景，但投资者不确定这一次他们会从沃什那里得到什么。
沃什坚称，他希望向金融市场提供更少的关于美联储将如何处理利率的线索，希望市场对即将发布的经济和通胀数据做出更多反应，而不是对美联储发出的信号做出更多反应。
但美国银行经济学家表示，随着美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特上周宣布了这一举措，沃什现在掌握了主动权。他们表示，投资者对沃什谈论通胀以及美联储可能如何反应的期望很高，如果未能兑现，可能会导致债券收益率飙升。
在国外股市，世界大部分地区的指数均下跌。韩国综合股价指数下跌 3.1%，香港恒生指数下跌 1.9%，是涨幅最大的两股。
今年夏天，首尔成为全球波动最剧烈的地区之一，因为它由受益于人工智能热潮的两家科技巨头三星电子和 SK 海力士主导。
美联社商业作家米歇尔·查普曼和伊莱恩·库尔滕巴赫为本报告做出了贡献。

item.title: 中国的工人在适应人工智能对就业日益增长的影响时担心被取代
item.description:
HONG KONG (AP) — Computer programmer Fei Zhaojun’s boss asked him if artificial intelligence could soon replace humans in coding jobs. Two weeks later, he was laid off from his job in Beijing, together with about 160 of his colleagues.
It’s an increasingly common scenario as artificial intelligence, supported by government policies, reshapesChina’smassive job market. Some economists believe that might eventually undermine the overall strength of the world’s second largest economy.
Rapid adoption of AI in many fields, from computer programmers to script writing and physical tasks, is pushing people out of their jobs or leaving them afraid that it might. China is at thevanguard of AI adoptionas governmentpoliciesencourage people and businesses to use AI applications androboticsin all aspects of life, so people like Fei are figuring out how to adapt.
“There appears to be far less anti-AI sentiment in China (than elsewhere). Most people seem either positive, neutral, or mildly interested in AI,” said Shujing He, a Beijing-based senior analyst at advisory and research firm Plenum.
“Individuals who worry about being replaced, as well as those who have already left traditional workplaces, are often eager to experiment with AI-enabled businesses and independent ventures,” she said. “The level of interest is striking.”
Until recently, Fei had doubted AI could do programming work perfectly, even though his bosses thought it was close enough.
“Mid-level coders’ job are essentially replaceable in most of the cases,” said Fei, 40. “Even if it is a disaster that leads to replacing all humans, at this stage, you just have to use it as everyone else is using it.”
Now he’s making vlog-style short videos during a career break while figuring out what he wants to do next. He’s not making a living off of his videos, which are about ordinary people’s lives, but hopes that they might help others.
Du Qinchun, a part-time translator, has been helping to train an AI model to do translations. That’s brought him more work, at least temporarily.
“But it’s true that the pay in the industry has been cut by more than half compared to what it was years ago,” said Du, who is based in southwestern China’s Chengdu city.
The trend is so evident that popular college programs in foreign languages have increasingly fallen out of favor as AI-powered translation tools have become more widespread.
The share of Chinese industrial enterprises saying they use AI models and “agents” jumped to 47.5% last year from 9.6% in 2024, according to the market intelligence firm IDC.
“China’s vibrant open-source model ecosystem fosters greater AI application innovation in industrial settings, gradually closing the gap between foundational model capabilities and real-world enterprise value creation,” said Yanze Du, an IDC senior research manager in Beijing.
Humanoid robots can now, for example, sort parcels in postal centers, although still on a small-scale basis, and are pushing the boundaries inperformingmore human tasks such as directing traffic and making coffee. Food delivery robots are also gaining ground across the country, potentially threatening the livelihoods of millions of Chinese food delivery workers.
GenerativeAIincreasingly is used for creation, production and distribution in China’s short drama industry. The number of live-action short and vertical video series designed for mobile phones fell about 75% in the first quarter of this year from a year earlier, according to Chinese media reports.
“Tasks that once required specialized training can now be performed by almost anyone with access to AI tools. This is particularly evident in software development and multimedia creation,” said Plenum’s He. “As a result, workers whose roles are narrowly concentrated in these areas may face greater displacement risk.”
A report from International Labor Organization, meanwhile, found that women face higher risks of losing employment due to use of AI than men, as they tend to work in areas more suitable for automation, such as assembling electronics, and remain underrepresented in science and technology.
Under China’s “AI Plus” initiative and itsfive-year planthrough 2030, the government is pushing to infuse AI across many industries, aiming to gain an edge in China’s technology rivalry with the U.S.
“What is specific to China is that the government is really into diffusing AI across the economy, so AI may get into different domains more quickly comparing to other countries,” said Zilan Qian, a research associate at Oxford China Policy Lab.
China’s economic growth has already beenslowing. Consumer spending has lagged partly due to people becoming reluctant to spend because they’re worried about losing their jobs. It’s added to problems stemming from aprolonged downturn in the housing marketthat has undermined household wealth.
China’s tech industries may be innovative with high productivity, but they may not generate many new jobs, said Eswar Prasad, a professor of economics and trade policy at Cornell University.
“AI is likely to lift productivity across the board but could have a severe disruptive effect on employment, worsening the employment growth problem and resulting in a detrimental effect on social stability,” he said.
Similar to their U.S. rivals, Chinese tech giants have cut or restructured tens of thousands ofjobs,partly due to AI. The outlook for the broader jobs market remains uncertain: China’s overall urban unemployment rate hovers around 5%, but unemployment for people aged 16 to 24, excluding students, is roughly triple that.
That said, in the longer run, some experts say unemployment rates could fall, since China’s population of 1.4 billion is rapidly aging andshrinking.
By 2050, China is projected to have fewer than two working-age adults to support each retiree, compared with more than 2.5 in the U.S., said Xuenan Cao, a professor at San Francisco Bay University whose focus includes technology and society.
“Automation could partially offset a shrinking workforce rather than being purely a threat to it,” Cao said.
Wang Zhicheng, 32, often used AI for brainstorming and fact-checking in his previous job as a scriptwriter for a company that produces 3D animated educational videos and interactive exercises for children.
After its parent company laid off roughly half of its 13 script writers, he chose to resign and work independently, making illustrated children’s books.
While AI sometimes saved time the scripts it generated, they often felt strange, Wang said. Episodes tended to be repetitive and formulaic and the level of detail devoted to knowledge varied widely.
“You can treat AI as a tool just like (Microsoft) Word,” said Wang, who has started his own studio making picture books and other creative works. “Humans are still the decision makers on which one to pick or pursue among all that AI generates.”
High school chemistry teacher Yang Zheng said he doesn’t consider AI as a threat to his job even though students use AI for help with their homework.
“Teachers cannot be there all the time,” he said. “It is a good thing for students as it generates in real-time so that students can ask follow-up questions,” said Yang, 29. “It often gets things wrong, but it improves over time.”
Fu Ting reported from Washington. AP video producer Wu Jia in Beijing contributed to this story.
